title: Why Your Phone Battery Dies Faster Every Year 🔋 #shorts
description:
Your phone runs on a lithium-ion battery. Charging pushes lithium ions from one side of the battery to the other, and using the phone lets them flow back. Every charge cycle, a few ions get trapped in a thin layer that slowly builds up inside, so fewer ions are left to carry charge. That's why capacity drops over time, often to around 80% after a few hundred full cycles. Heat and sitting at 100% speed it up, so avoid heat and use your phone's optimized or limited charging.

lines: Your phone lasted all day when it was new. Now it's dead by lunch.
Inside is a lithium-ion battery. Charging pushes lithium ions to one side. Using your phone lets them flow back, and that flow is your power.
But every cycle, a few ions get stuck in a thin layer that slowly builds up inside. Stuck ions can't carry charge anymore.
Fewer moving ions means less capacity. After a few hundred full charges, many batteries are down to around eighty percent.
Heat and sitting at a hundred percent make it worse. So keep it cool, and turn on optimized charging.
Every charge traps a few ions. That's why batteries age.
